To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

performance-aware behavioral equivalences can be used to detect performance and functional dependencies and then to pinpoint the metrics at the root of a balanced trade-off between security and performance.

(i) the notion of behavioral equivalence is a powerful tool for the verification of secure and performance-aware systems, (ii) it is possible to define performance-aware notions of weak behavioral equivalence, which are suitable for the analysis of component-based systems, (iii) these notions of weak behavioral equivalences allow to identify functional dependencies among components as well as to study the quantitative effect of such dependencies on the system behavior, (iv) these equivalences can be used to detect the presence of security/performance

the use of performance-based notions of behavioral equivalence is a viable approach for the development of predictive techniques that are capable of detecting functional dependencies and pinpointing the metrics of interest for performance analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and the application of a methodology for verifying the security, the performance, and the tradeoffs between these properties of component-based systems.
the study of performance-aware notions and their use in a predictive approach to the analysis of component-based systems.
the definition, formalization and application of weak behavioral equivalences for component-based systems, in order to achieve a balanced trade-off among security and performance aspects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a performance-aware notion of behavioral equivalence is a promising approach to achieve an effective and efficient tradeoff among security and performance requirements.

a component-based system can be considered secure and performance-aware only if it can be proved secure and performance-aware, where these two properties are formalized by the use of performance-based notions of behavioral equivalence.
a weak behavioral equivalence is a formal means for identifying functional and performance dependencies in the system, and then for identifying the metrics at the core of a balanced trade-off.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of behavioral equivalences for security and performance analysis of component-based systems is a powerful approach to achieve a balanced trade-off among the various requirements of these systems.

we have developed a formal framework for the analysis of component-based systems, which is based upon a set of behavioral equivalence notions, and we have used such a framework for the analysis and verification of secure and performance-aware component-based systems.

we have proposed a novel notion of behavioral equivalence that is based on a quantitative notion of distance between system behaviors and we have shown how to use it to detect functional dependencies and to study their quantitative impact on the system performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of security and performance requirements, the use of behavioral equivalences for component verification can no longer be based on the standard notion of bisimulation, but it has to be based on the use of a more general notion of equivalence, which takes into account the presence of performance-aware metrics.
the performance-aware notion of behavioral equivalence is not unique, since it depends on the performance model used to quantify the performance aspects of interest.

the use of a single equivalence notion is not sufficient to capture the interplay of functional and performance dependencies in component-based systems, and that the use of different behavioral equivalences is required to reveal all the dependencies of interest.
